data.name: Ramavtar
data.short_meaning: God in the form of Ram, with the qualities of a king or ruler
data.long_meaning: Ram means 'God' and Avtar means 'manifestation' or 'descent'. This name is often given to a child born during the nine-day festival of Ram Navami, which is dedicated to Lord Ram, one of the principal deities of Hinduism. Ram is known for his courage, strength, and righteousness, and is considered an ideal of masculine power and leadership.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine qualities of a ruler or king, and is a reminder of the divine presence within us all
data.numerology_meaning: Represents harmony and balance, and is a number of love and relationships

in_sanskrit.long_meaning: रामके वतारनाम (Rāmakē vatārānām) - Manifestation/incarnation of Lord Rama.

in_tamil.name: ராமவதர்

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Ramavtar' is deeply rooted in Hindu culture and carries a rich legacy. It is a reminder of Lord Ram, the paragon of virtues and an embodiment of power, strength, and righteousness. Ramayana, an ancient Sanskrit epic, is one of the two major Indian epics and speaks of Lord Ram and his life. This name embodies the ideals of masculinity, leadership, and morality , inspiring generations of Hindus.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the belief in Avtar, or the manifestation of God on Earth, is an important tenet. 'Ramavtar' signifies the belief in God's presence in every being. It's a reminder that the Divine is not just an abstract concept, but a living, breathing reality that can be experienced and felt. The name 'Ramavtar' also symbolizes faith, reverence, and devotion towards the divine being. Through this name, one is spiritually connected to the eternal and unchanging divine consciousness, Ram.

historical_references.reference: Ramavtar was an epithet of Lord Rama, a central figure in the Indian epic Ramayana. This epic narrates the journey of Lord Rama in exile, his battle against the demon king Ravana, and his eventual return to his kingdom.

The name Ramavtar is also used as a personal name for individuals in Hindu culture, particularly in North India. It is derived from the name Rama and the Sanskrit word 'isvara', meaning 'god' or 'supreme ruler'.
